lock_refresh.scope: Latest versions satisfying the existing stable and optional dependency bounds

strict_frontier.interpretation: The version-2 report separates minimum-supported, locked, latest-compatible, latest-overall, upper-bound preview, prerelease, and support-window facts. Strict mode passes because every direct requirement is locked at its latest compatible final release and there are no policy violations; excluded release families remain isolated preview candidates rather than false stale-floor failures.

security_and_licence.cargo_deny: advisories, licences, bans, and sources passed with one duplicate syn-version warning
security_and_licence.python_licence_gate: Hosted dependency-review has a deny list; no equivalent lock-complete local Python licence policy gate is currently enforced.

findings.summary: The strict dependency-frontier command conflates compatibility floors with resolved versions and cannot distinguish an intentionally broad supported range from a stale lock.
findings.required_disposition: Report minimum-supported, locked, latest-compatible, latest-overall, upper-bound blocker, prerelease, and support-window status separately; make strict mode fail only on policy violations.
findings.resolution: scripts/dependency_frontier.py now emits the separated version-2 report and the live strict audit passes with 60 of 60 direct requirements locked at their latest compatible final release.

findings.summary: Core upper bounds exclude SciPy 1.18, pandas 3.0, and xarray 2026 without a current compatibility report, while the JAX, Griffe, and Ruff lanes also stop before their latest release families.
findings.required_disposition: Exercise each blocked family in an isolated preview resolution and record breaking changes, numerical/serialization effects, performance, and rollback before promotion or renewed exclusion.

findings.summary: Python licence enforcement is hosted-only and is not reproduced locally against the exact runtime lock; the ad hoc installed-environment report also includes development packages.
findings.required_disposition: Generate a lock-derived runtime SBOM/licence report locally and apply the same reviewed allow/deny policy as hosted dependency review.
findings.resolution: scripts/run_python_license_audit.sh exports the frozen runtime-only lock, installs it in an isolated environment, records resolved licence metadata, and applies the same GPL/AGPL deny list as hosted dependency review with missing licences failing closed; the 34-package runtime report passes.

findings.summary: Bandit reports 13 low-severity runtime asserts whose behavior disappears under Python optimization, including checks on ingestion and method control-flow invariants.
findings.required_disposition: Replace security- or correctness-relevant asserts with explicit typed failures; justify purely internal narrowing asserts and keep the scanner at zero unreviewed findings.
findings.resolution: All 13 runtime assertions were replaced with explicit typed or invariant failures, the affected 269-test behavioral slice passed, and the configured recursive Bandit scan reports zero findings across 59,325 lines.

findings.summary: Cargo resolves both syn 2 and syn 3 through PyO3 and Serde; cargo-deny allows this duplicate but records it as a dependency-footprint warning.
findings.required_disposition: Track upstream convergence and retain the duplicate only while both dependency chains are necessary and advisories/licences remain clean.

findings.summary: Preview runtimes and major dependency families have no unified non-blocking compatibility workflow or machine-readable promotion/rollback receipt.
findings.required_disposition: Add named preview matrices and a promotion receipt that requires stable CPU fallback, numerical equivalence, Arrow round trips, security, provenance, and measured benefit.
findings.resolution: The scheduled and manually dispatchable dependency-preview workflow isolates every upper-bound family, Python 3.15, cargo-nextest, and sccache as continue-on-error observations, while the frozen promotion policy defines the machine-readable candidate, promotion, and rollback receipt.

findings.summary: The refreshed PyArrow 25 lane emits a deprecation warning for the DataFrame interchange conversion used by the SDK; current Arrow guidance prefers the Arrow PyCapsule interface where producers support it.
findings.required_disposition: Add PyCapsule-first conversion with an explicitly tested DataFrame-protocol fallback, preserving allow-copy, nullable, categorical, timezone, schema, and provenance semantics.

findings.summary: The public top-level import eagerly reaches jsonschema format dependencies and constructs rfc3987 parsers, breaching the 5 second reviewer smoke budget by more than threefold in repeated isolated probes.
findings.required_disposition: Lazy-load validation-only dependencies, profile cold and warm imports, and retain the stable top-level symbols and error behavior while restoring the import budget.
findings.resolution: The public package surface now uses static lazy exports without importing validation-only schema dependencies; three isolated probes completed in 3.63, 4.02, and 4.05 seconds while the stable symbol and error contracts passed.
